take.thing: The camera never cuts: each room is a new framing from one lens height joined by a short push in, never a fade to white.
take.why: It makes the visitor feel they walk through one home, so every piece is seen in a real room.

native.palette: grey, white text, one red accent

left_out: the floating parts and the red keycap
the loop and the orange button
differences: Photos of rooms, not a keyboard
Four rooms instead of one object
A push in of about 600 ms with no 3D in the browser
sources.removal: The rooms become four separate photos that fade between each other and feel like a catalogue.

take.thing: A small piece stands alone on a rug in an empty room, framed through a blurred foreground arm of another chair.
take.why: It gives depth and calm with no graphic, so the piece looks owned not displayed.

native.palette: bone room, olive chair, walnut arm

left_out: the made for your project headline
differences: We keep the same camera spot across four rooms
No headline sits on the photo of the room
Our piece can be bought by tapping it
sources.removal: The rooms lose their depth and read as flat stock photos.

take.thing: The section headline sits in the empty wall of the room photo at the left gutter with the room names in a quiet row under it.
take.why: It tells the visitor where they are before any product competes for attention.

native.type: one serif headline, tiny spaced capitals

left_out: the three product cards on pale grey
the olive sofa and the AI light
differences: Four room names as a switcher, not a fixed photo
Headline is short and the photo moves
The product row is not under it
sources.removal: The headline floats over a busy photo and the switcher has no home.
